summary: The root ذأم (dhAm) primarily signifies blame, censure, or finding fault with someone or something. It implies a strong disapproval or disparagement, often leading to disgrace or contempt.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: َأَمَهُ, (T, S, M, Msb, K,) aor. َأََ, (S, M, Msb, K,) inf. n. َأْمٌ, (S, * M,) He blamed, or found fault with, him, or it; (T, S, Msb;) namely, a man, (T, [in which it is said that َأَمْتُهُ in the sense of عِبْتُهُ is more common than َمَمْتُهُ, ” though the contr.

ا أمهُ, (TA,) inf. n. إِ ْآمٌ, (K, TA,) He frightened him, or terrified him; syn. of the inf. n. رُعْبٌ. (K, TA.) أَ ْأَمْتَنِى عَلَى كَ َا Thou compelledst me against my will to do such a thing. (Fr, S.)
َأْمٌ i. q. عَيْبٌ [as a subst., meaning A vice, fault, defect, or the like; like َامٌ, without ء, and َيْمٌ; as well as an inf. n. of 1, q. v.]: with and without ء (S.)
َأْمَةٌ A word: so in the saying, مَا سَمِعْتُ لَهُ َأْمَةً [ I heard not a word that he had to utter]. (K.)
مَ ْؤُومٌ pass. part. n. of 1. (S, Msb.) مَ ْؤُومًا in the Kur [vii. 17] means Blamed: (TA:) or driven away: (M, TA:) or, accord. to Lh and Mujáhid, banished. (T, TA. *)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
